posts.audience: Newer cash-game players who play too many hands from early position
posts.hook: The button is the best seat at the table. Here's why.
posts.caption:
The button is the best seat at the table, and it isn't close.

You act last on every street after the flop. That means you see what everyone else does before you decide, and you get to pick the size of the pot.

That's why good players open far more hands on the button than under the gun. Same cards, very different spot.

Save this for your next session. Which seat do you find hardest to play?

#poker #pokerstrategy #texasholdem #cashgame

posts.audience: Players who chase losses or play above their bankroll
posts.hook: Most bankrolls don't die from bad luck. They die from one bad night.
posts.caption:
Most bankrolls don't go broke from a downswing. They go broke from one night of chasing it.

A few rules that keep a bad session from becoming a bad month:

• Decide your stop before you sit down
• Never move up to win it back
• Write the result down, even when it hurts

Which one do you break most? Be honest.

#poker #bankrollmanagement #pokermindset #pokerlife

posts.audience: Players who use one 3-bet size everywhere
posts.hook: Your 3-bet size should depend on your seat.
posts.caption:
One 3-bet size for every spot is leaving money on the table.

A common starting point in cash games:
• In position: about 3 times the open
• Out of position: about 4 times the open

Out of position you play the rest of the hand at a disadvantage, so you make it more expensive to call.

Starting points, not laws. Save it for your next session.

#poker #pokerstrategy #cashgame #pokertips
posts.coverAlt: Reel cover: How big should your 3-bet be? The answer depends on your position.

steps.title: In position
steps.body:
About *3×* the open.
They raise 3 BB, you make it about 9.

steps.title: Out of position
steps.body:
About *4×* the open.
They raise 3 BB, you make it about 12.

steps.title: Why bigger?
steps.body: Out of position you play every street at a disadvantage. Make calling cost more.
